adds.rationale: Russia's invasion of Ukraine triggered a concrete, dated buildup-phase signal for the defense/rearmament wave the profile names under geopolitical realignment: aerospace-defense ETFs rallied double digits in a week with accelerating inflows, while Germany and other NATO allies announced structural defense-budget increases.

news_evidence.summary: iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense ETF (ITA) and peers gained nearly double-digits in the week following Russia's Feb 24 invasion; ITA up 5%+ since the invasion
Defense-sector ETFs hauled in $126M of inflows in the week to Feb 21, almost doubling their 2022 YTD total, as the Ukraine crisis raised the prospect of higher military spending
Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman shares up roughly 20% as war stocks surge; Germany announces defense budget will rise above 2% of GDP

rationale_overall: The watchlist stays AI-heavy (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, NVDA, SPY all kept) because Q1 2022 news shows the big-tech names still executing on thesis, not cresting: Apple posted a record $123.9B quarter, Microsoft announced the $68.7B Activision deal, Alphabet announced a 20-for-1 split, and Nvidia's terminated Arm acquisition is a regulatory setback but not a thesis breach for its core AI/semiconductor business. The single add, ITA, fills the geopolitical/defense-and-rearmament wave with clean dated evidence of a buildup move; it brings the watchlist to the 6-ticker cap. No removes this quarter: no incumbent shows a fundamental thesis breach or peak-enthusiasm signal yet.
